text:
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(spl): SplFileObject could not open a file, said so three times, and handed it back anyway

`new SplFileObject($p)` is php's way of saying "open this or fail loudly". elephc
failed QUIETLY. MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6 against a missing file:

    php    : RuntimeException: SplFileObject::__construct(nope.txt): Failed to open
             stream: No such file or directory
    elephc : Warning: fopen(nope.txt): Failed to open stream: …
             Warning: file(nope.txt): Failed to open stream: …
             Warning: foreach() argument must be of type array|object, false given
             …and a live object whose stream was `false`

Three warnings php never prints, no exception, and a program that carried on
reading nothing. A DIRECTORY is worse still: php refuses it before opening anything
and does so as a `LogicException`, because an `SplFileObject` cannot wrap one at
all; elephc opened it and warned about bytes it could not read.

The constructor now checks `is_dir()` first, opens the stream SUPPRESSED — which is
what removes the three warnings — and throws php's own wording when the open failed.
The reason is approximated from `file_exists()`, the way `DirectoryIterator` already
does here: the synthesized body is PHP, has no `errno`, and `error_get_last()`,
which would carry php's text verbatim, is not implemented.

THE LINES NOW COME FROM THE STREAM, not from the path. `file($this->backingPath)`
re-opened the file by NAME, and a stream with no name to re-open came back EMPTY
every time — `new SplFileObject("php://memory", "r+")` answered nothing at all after
a write, and a file appended to through its own handle iterated stale content. The
read costs what `fgets()` costs, which is no longer a reason to avoid it: the same
900 KB file went from 538 ms to 20 ms when the line reader learned to fill the
stream's buffer. The position is saved and restored, because reloading is not a seek
the program asked for.

Verified: 272 `spl::`, 1097 `io::` and 50 csv tests pass, and the 183-program round-8
corpus is unchanged at 180 identical.

Known residual: `SplFileInfo::openFile()` on a missing file throws with
`SplFileObject::__construct(…)` in the message where php names
`SplFileInfo::openFile(…)`; php opens the stream inside `openFile()` and elephc
delegates to the constructor. `SplTempFileObject` keeps its own in-memory model and
still differs from php on the trailing newline and on `valid()` — a separate sub-model
with its own bodies, not this constructor.
MSG
